Why did leave you reddit, if you were a user before and what was the final straw?
How important is freedom of speech on online platforms to you? If it is/is not, would you mind saying why?

They cite reasons of rioting, racism, hate speech, and even terrorism type activity as justifications. I will not name the governments, nor the cases or politics behind such controversies. Do you think having a voice here leads to democracy? What kind of implications do online life have for democratic ideals? Feel free to expand, discuss or let me know what you feel. This is mostly a feeler for me as I plan to do much research outside of the voat realm, but am really interested in what you have to say. I find that these subjects are incredibly important for our society since the lines between online and offline life and identities are increasingly moving towards a blurry mirage.

I will also answer any questions you have for me, if you happen to have them and will be regularly checking back.
